fields.Name: ORD-46 - Service Period Lock
fields.Description: A blank service period may be FILLED IN on the order of a CLOSED deal, while a date that is already set still meets the lock (SP1-SP5). The deal lock refuses order-line edits while the deal is closed, and its refusal names what it protects: what was sold. Service dates are the coverage window rather than the thing, and a blank one is the field a rep must be able to set on a Won deal's order — ConfirmEligibility will not confirm a line whose product requires a service period until it carries both a start and an end, while Sales can state only a term start on a deal line, so the end can only be set here. A date that is already set had a source, and moving it changes the window agreed at the close, so it still goes through reopening. The unit suite pins which saves consult the veto; this bundle proves the exempt save actually lands against a live database, and that each bound holds.

ExpectedOutcomes.summary: With a veto registered that refuses every edit: SP1 a save filling ServicePeriodStart and ServicePeriodEnd on an unbooked order goes through and the stored row really carries the new dates. SP2 the same save carrying a quantity change is refused, says the deal is closed, and leaves no part of itself behind — neither the quantity nor the dates. SP3 a dates-only save on a line whose order has booked is refused, because by then the stored period is the settled term recognition is derived from; the line is reloaded rather than reused, so the check meets the lock rather than the bypass Orders' own write paths set. SP4 a save that MOVES dates the line already carried is refused and the stored period is unchanged, which is the fill-versus-change bound proved on the row rather than on the verdict. SP5 the reported shape — the line already carries the start and only the end is filled — goes through, and the start is untouched.
